title: Thoracolumbar FSU disc pressure under 500 N compression (centric/eccentric) and shear

quantity.name: IDP
quantity.definition: nucleus-centre pressure at 500 N peak load (mean ± SD over specimens)

source.authors: Frei H, Oxland TR, Nolte LP
source.sample: human cadaver thoracolumbar FSUs, no degeneration observed; 12 specimens (11 T12-L1, 1 L1-L2 FSUs)

protocol.summary: FSUs mounted in PMMA (disc horizontal), servo-hydraulic machine (MTS Bionix). Compression series to 500 N at 50 N/s, 10 s hold, unload: pure compression at the balance point and flexion-, extension-, right- and left-lateral compression with 2.0 cm load eccentricity; shear series (posterior, anterior, left, right) to 500 N at 50 N/s through the centre of shear (~mid-disc) in a jig allowing unconstrained motion. Disc pressure: 2.1 mm needle (Denton) with sensing part in the centre of the nucleus; values at peak load averaged.
how_to_simulate: Model the FSU with vertebrae potted; inferior vertebra fixed, superior free (unconstrained).
Apply 500 N compression at the balance point, or 500 N with 20 mm anterior/posterior/lateral eccentricity, or 500 N shear through mid-disc height (posterior/anterior/left/right).
Report nucleus-centre pressure at peak load (and axial/shear translation of the upper vertebra).
protocol.notes: Disc pressure in Fig 2 trace starts at ~0 at zero load; whether the sensor was zeroed in the unloaded state is not stated, treated as absolute. Endplate and rim strains (Figs 4-7) not extracted.

extraction.from: Fig 3 (bars mean, error bars SD); text: compression mean 0.48 (SD 0.1), posterior shear 0.23 (SD 0.10)
extraction.check_notes: Pixel digitisation of bar tops and SD caps. Checks: mean of 5 compression bars 0.480 vs text 0.48; posterior shear 0.231 (SD 0.097) vs text 0.23 (SD 0.10). n per bar assumed 12 (pressure analysis on all specimens; strain analysis excluded 3).
